title: The Lindström-Gessel-Viennot Lemma
description: The LGV Lemma: determinants of binomial coefficient matrices count non-intersecting lattice path tuples, unifying classical combinatorial identities.

overview.summary: The Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) Lemma is a cornerstone theorem in enumerative combinatorics, establishing that determinants of binomial coefficient matrices always count combinatorial objects — namely, non-intersecting lattice path tuples.
overview.keyInsight: For strictly ordered source positions a₁ < ... < aᵣ and target positions b₁ < ... < bᵣ, the matrix M with Mᵢⱼ = C(m + bⱼ - aᵢ, m) has its determinant equal to the number of non-intersecting r-tuples of lattice paths. This is proved via the Gessel-Viennot sign-reversing involution (formalized in BallotProblemOQ03OQ02.lean).
overview.mathematicalContent: The file presents the LGV theorem and verifies it for concrete 2×2 examples. For m=2 with sources [0,1] and targets [2,3], the path matrix [[6,10],[3,6]] has det = 36-30 = 6, matching the 6 non-intersecting path pairs. For m=3 with sources [0,1] and targets [3,4], the matrix [[20,35],[10,20]] has det = 400-350 = 50.

sections.title: Main Theorem
sections.content: The LGV Lemma: `niTupleCount = det(pathMatrix)` for well-formed configurations.

sections.title: 1×1 Case
sections.content: The 1×1 determinant is simply the path count C(m + b - a, m).

sections.title: 2×2 Concrete Examples
sections.content: For m=2, det=6 paths; for m=3, det=50 paths. Both verified by computation.

sections.title: Non-Negativity and Well-Formedness
sections.content: The determinant is always non-negative (it counts path tuples). Well-formedness is essential.
